- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.7) and forecast is rising sharply, reduce forecast peak to avoid over-optimism.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤-0.3) and forecast is falling, avoid excessive downward correction — allow slight lagged rebound.  
- If recent price history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days trending down), model should not overcorrect upward.  
- Overshoots after spikes (especially >10% above recent high) should be capped or smoothed with sentiment-weighted dampening.  
- Forecast horizon 30d: if sentiment is volatile or mixed, reduce forecast variance — don’t assume trend continuation.  
- If sentiment history shows strong recent divergence from price (e.g., sentiment up but price down), adjust forecast to reflect sentiment lag.  
- When sentiment is high but price is flat or declining, forecast should not assume continuation — expect mean reversion or reversal.  
- Avoid forecasting extreme values (±15% from recent range) unless sentiment strongly supports it — use sentiment as a soft constraint.
